newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes at fresh low, looks weak.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes at fresh low, looks weak.

text.p: Gold prices fixed at a fresh near-12-year low on Wednesday, leading dealers to forecast tests of the week's lowest traded prices.
A bounce from the lows struck on Monday was overcome by fresh selling from both speculators and, some dealers said, Australian gold producers.
Bullion was fixed at $315.75 an ounce versus $320.80 on Tuesday. It was its lowest fix since December 11, 1985.
Dealers said gold had become oversold so Tuesday's rebound in price became inevitable as speculators who had sold forward on the basis that prices would fall bought to take their profits.
However, the same speculators were then just as keen to re-invest on the assumption that prices would fall again, dealer said.
"The speculator selling was evident in New York and the Far East before Europe opened. The sentiment is still very negative," said one market analyst.
The strong and steady dollar and weaker platinum and palladium markets were adding to gold's woes, dealers said.
"They are under pressure and we have seen some reasonable selling but there seems to be some support at $315.00-$315.50, where there is some short covering by the professionals," one dealer said.
However, he warned that if that level fell, then a return was likely to the week's lows around $313.60, which had been tested in Europe and New York on Monday.
"That is a critical level," the dealer said.
Gold prices have collapsed since the Reserve Bank of Australia last Thursday said it had sold 167 tonnes of gold from its reserves over the past six months.
The announcement brought heavy investor and speculator selling of gold on fears other banks might follow the example.
It also provoked criticism from the Australian gold mining industry, half of which is producing at a loss at these prices.
Prices have been under pressure all year in anticipation of sales by European central banks to help their countries achieve the entry criteria for European Monetary Union in 1999.
"A European central bank selling would be one thing, but the central bank of the world's third largest gold producer is even more bearish for the market," one market analyst said.
Central bank gold reserves total over 28,000 tonnes.
Silver prices were also weak on Wednesday and were indicated at $4.26/$4.28, around their lowest level since March 1995.
Platinum dipped to under $400 for the first time since early June as dealers anticipated a resumption of Russian exports.

It was $14.00 lower at $396.00/$400.00 and sister metal palladium was $4.00 down at $1270.00/$174.00, also in anticipation of Russia beginning its 1997 export campaign, delayed by adminstrative problems, this week.
The absence of Russian supplies of palladium earlier sent prices soaring to their highest level in 17 years.
Russian is the world's leading supplier of palladium and second largest exporter of platinum after South Afirca.
